newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-GROBBELAAR SAYS HE FAKED MATCH-RIGGING CONFESSION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GROBBELAAR SAYS HE FAKED MATCH-RIGGING CONFESSION.

text.p: Former Liverpool goalkeeper Bruce Grobbelaar said on Thursday he had falsely admitted to rigging matches in a bid to trick a former business partner who had suggested he try to throw games.
Grobbelaar denied he had ever thrown a soccer match, saying he had only been paid for forecasting the results of games.
"Soccer is a business. You don't go onto the field to lose a game," he told a court in the southern English town of Winchester.

The prosecution's case that Grobbelaar and three others rigged games to benefit an Asian betting syndicate rests largely on covert films recorded in October 1994 in which the keeper appeared to admit that he had rigged matches.

The tapes were recorded by Chris Vincent as part of a sting operation intended to make Grobbelaar incriminate himself. Vincent asked the keeper if he would throw games for the benefit of another, mythical syndicate.
"He said to me: 'You must have thrown games in the past'. I thought, why not agree with him and see what happens?" the Zimbabwean goalkeeper told a court in Winchester.
"Were you telling the truth?" asked Grobbelaar's lawyer Rodney Klevan.

"No. I told him that lie to get his confidence and to tell him what he wanted to hear. I wanted to know who he was working with," said Grobbelaar, who lost 60,000 pounds when a safari park venture he and Vincent were running folded in July 1994.
Grobbelaar is accused along with former Wimbledon keeper Hans Segers, ex-Wimbledon and Aston Villa striker John Fashanu and Malaysian businessman Heng Suan Lim of rigging games.
Asked by Klevan about what seemed to be damaging admissions made on the tapes, Grobbelaar repllied :"That was me putting a bit of spice into it, a little innuendo."
"This has been hanging over the four of us here for two years and three months and still the same thing comes out -- that we are here because we have been throwing games.

"We'll see at the end of it. There is no way I have ever thrown a game," Grobbelaar said in a loud, clear voice. Like Segers before him, he admitted to forecasting the results of matches in return for cash from Lim.
One of the main accusations against Grobbelaar is that he accepted 40,000 pounds from Fashanu in late November 1993 for rigging a game against Newcastle which Liverpool lost 3-0.
The court was shown extracts of the game, in which Newcastle striker Andy Cole scored a first-half hat-trick.
"Could you have done anything about those goals?" Klevan asked Grobbelaar, who transferred from Liverpool to Southampton in August 1994.

"If you'd got a board and boarded up the goal, you could have," the keeper replied to laughter in court. The court was then shown extracts from three other games where Grobbelaar was alleged to have had an interest in fixing the results.
Asked about one ball he let slip through his arms into the net during between Manchester City and Southampton, he said:

"You do let in some goals you're disappointed with. The opponent is five or six yards (metres) away, the ball is travelling at 50 or 60 mph (85 to 100 kph), and it's very hard to get your hand to it in time."

Vincent said Grobbelaar had given him 20,000 pounds from the Newcastle money and asked him to pay off various debts. But the keeper said he had given Vincent the money a week earlier and told him to buy property in South Africa with it.

Asked by Klevan where the 20,000 pounds had come from, Grobbelaar said it was the proceeds from coaching spells abroad and after-dinner speeches. He kept the money in his sock drawer, he told the court.
